title: Cost and capacity incident
problem: A workload's daily cost triples while latency and error rate also increase; the team must contain impact without blindly removing resilience capacity.

requirements.availability: Mitigation must preserve the customer SLO and minimum failure headroom
requirements.security: Cost investigation uses read-only evidence and preserves auditability
requirements.cost: Return unit cost to the approved range and prevent recurrence

architecture.summary: Cost allocation, usage telemetry, anomaly alerts and workload performance data are correlated by owner, service, operation and deployment.
data_flow: Billing and usage to cost analytics

decisions: Cost anomalies are operational signals with named owners
Investigation roles are read-only and remediation remains reviewed
Do not reduce below tested failover headroom during containment
Correlate saturation and scaling before resizing
Track cost per successful business transaction
Remove redundant work and idle capacity after reliability review

failure_modes.impact: Compute, network and dependency cost rise while latency worsens
failure_modes.detection: Request amplification, retry count and cost anomaly
failure_modes.mitigation: Bound retries, add jitter/backpressure and protect dependency
failure_modes.prevention: Retry budgets, load/failure tests and circuit breakers

failure_modes.impact: Capacity churn, instability and unnecessary cost
failure_modes.detection: Frequent scale events and metric lag
failure_modes.prevention: Representative load tests and multi-signal scaling review

decisions.decision: Optimize unit economics after identifying the workload driver
decisions.trade_off: Requires allocation and business-volume data beyond the AWS bill

decisions.decision: Preserve tested failover minimum during emergency cost containment
decisions.trade_off: Some spend remains while availability risk is controlled
decisions.revisit_when: Business accepts a different reliability target
